 NCAN’s FAFSA Tracker’s 10th Year Launches as US Pushes to Extend FAFSA Record
 October 19, 2026 
 Two minutes 
 Share 
 By Bill DeBaun, Senior Director, Data and Strategic Initiatives 
 Share 
 Copy Link 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 X 
 Facebook 
 The National College Attainment Network's (NCAN's)  FAFSA Tracker marks a decade of service to the field as the United States seeks to further extend record-setting FAFSA, or Free Application for Federal Student Aid, completion gains for the high school class of 2027. Coming on the heels of the class of 2026, which achieved 59.1% FAFSA completion nationally by June 30, practitioners and policymakers alike will be working toward further gains that connect students with financial aid for education and training after high school. 
 The 2027-28 FAFSA cycle Tracker is now live with data through October 9. 
 The class of 2027 is well-positioned to push past last year’s record highs. The 2027-28 FAFSA cycle (recall that FAFSA cycles correspond to the years in which the financial aid is received , not the academic year in which the form is completed) has already been open since September 24, the earliest opening on record . 
 The vibe shift around the FAFSA over the past two years has been profound. After the class of 2024 experienced significant difficulties with the rollout of the new platform, the past two graduating classes have bounced back significantly and set all new highs nationally and in most states. The now “surprisingly delightful FAFSA,” according to some observers’ appellations, has reduced the average FAFSA completion time to 15 minutes or less while also expanding Pell Grant eligibility and increasing the number of maximum Pell Grant recipients. 
 NCAN launched its FAFSA Tracker way back in 2017 to better understand FAFSA completion patterns at the national, state, and local levels. A decade later, now with well over 1 million views, NCAN’s FAFSA Tracker is a nationally trusted source for understanding FAFSA completion trends within and across cycles. 
 NCAN’s FAFSA Tracker visualizes data at the national, state, and local levels and is based on data released weekly from Federal Student Aid. 
 In honor of our FAFSA Tracker’s decade mark, we’ve refreshed its aesthetics and simplified its functionality. Longtime users will notice a more browser-friendly format, better help text, and streamlined functionality, but if anything looks amiss users are welcome to email [email protected] . 
 Recapping the Class of 2026 
 The 2026-27 cycle Tracker for the high school class of 2026 has seen its last update. After 52 weeks, through September 25, 2026, the estimated national FAFSA completion rate is 64.6%, an all-time high for the Tracker. The number of FAFSAs completed grew by 7.5% year-over-year, an increase of more than 185,000 additional applications. 
 The top five states for percent of seniors completing were Tennessee (76.6%), Mississippi (75.6%), Illinois (74.7%), Texas (73.3%), and New Jersey (72.2%). Notably, six of the top 10 states by percent of seniors completing have implemented universal FAFSA policies that make FAFSA completion a requirement for high school graduation. 
 The five states with the largest year-over-year growth in applications included Alaska (+16.2%), New Mexico (+14.2%), Florida (+12.6%), Arizona (+12.6%), and North Carolina (+12.4%).
